title: Integration Clearinghouse — Weekly sync notes (standup raw)
content:
Meeting: Integration Clearinghouse weekly sync — raw notes
Date: 2026-06-29 10:00–10:45 PT
Location: Zoom / #se-proservices
Facilitator: Marissa Chen
Attendees: Marissa, Omar, Priya, Liam, Sofia, Jason (SRE), Anita (Customer Success)

Purpose: Triage in-flight integrations, surface blockers, confirm rollout windows and next actions for high-risk customers. Lightweight — capture action owners and short timelines.

---
Quick scoreboard (top risks this week)
- Aurelia Health: Data pipeline schema mismatch blocking sanity runs (High)
- Crux Analytics: Latency spike under burst tests after kv-cache enabled on staging (Medium-High)
- North Ridge Bank: Security review complete; waiting on on-prem packaging ETA (Medium)

---
Aurelia Health (owner: Priya)- Status: Staging ingress validated but nightly ETL failing on patient_metadata schema v2 -> v3 transform. Several rows rejected (400s) when writing to downstream store.
- Recent: Priya ran a focused ingest with sample subset; observed failure in column "encounter_summary" length > 64k causing JSON blob truncation in transform.
- Blocker: Upstream partner (Aurelia ETL team) sending legacy payloads intermittently; we need a compatibility shim or preprocessor.
- Risk level: High. This blocks their POC verification scheduled for 2026-07-06.
- Proposed immediate mitigations:
  - temporary preprocessor to truncate/encode long fields (Priya, ETA 2026-06-30)
  - add a new validation rule to ingest pipeline to surface offending records into a dead-letter S3 prefix for analysis (Omar, ETA 2026-07-01)
  - schedule a 30-min sync with Aurelia ETL lead to agree on schema contract (Marissa to set, target 2026-06-30)
- Open questions / notes to self:
  - confirm whether truncation is allowed from product/legal side (Anita to confirm by 2026-06-30)

Crux Analytics (owner: Liam)- Status: Feature-complete integration; running scale tests. After enabling prefix KV cache in staging, we saw median tail latency regressions for short-prompt requests under burst (95th moved from 220ms -> 480ms).
- Recent: SRE replayed production-like burst with same model variant and GPU profile. Hypothesis: cache warm-up thrashing when multiple small sessions hit different prefixes concurrently.
- Blocker: Can't reproduce with current synthetic harness; might be workload-specific (their traffic has many concurrent short chats).
- Action items:
  - Instrument cache hit/miss by session id for next test run (Jason, ETA 2026-07-01)
  - Rollback cache toggles to per-session cache on canary (Liam, ETA 2026-07-02)
  - Run controlled burst with real Crux trace ingestion (they agreed to a scrubbed trace; awaiting delivery)
- Notes:
  - Potential optimization: aggressive LRU with session affinity vs global prefix cache — engineering to sketch tradeoffs and cost impact (Liam/Omar, doc PR#2876)

North Ridge Bank (owner: Sofia)- Status: Enterprise security review completed. They want a private deploy (on-prem bundle) with HSM integration and FIPS components. Legal and procurement cleared main contract.
- Blocker: Packaging team reports third-party binary licensing conflict for a specific kernel optimizer used in our on-prem installer.
- Risk level: Medium — schedule slip possible if alternate optimizer needs validation.
- Actions:
  - Packaging to produce a minimal installer variant without the optimizer for initial handoff (Packaging owner: Vikram, ETA 2026-07-05)
  - Security to produce final attestation document for HSM/KMS usage (Anita, ETA 2026-07-02)
  - Plan a dry run install with their infra team week of 2026-07-12

Cross-customer items / Platform updates
- Canary rollout policy: Product asked for an explicit fallback policy when dedicated capacity node fails — we need a short runbook (Marissa/Omar to draft by 2026-07-03).
- Model variant propagation: observed mismatch between catalog metadata and deployed container labels in a recent Dedicated rollout. Root cause appears to be the deploy pipeline not updating two parallel metadata stores. Action: Jason to add a CI check that fails deploys when hashes diverge (ETA 2026-07-06).
- Observability ask: SEs want a per-customer route-level token cost and median latency view in Console for integrations in progress. Product agreed to prioritize a minimal dashboard (PM: Clara). Prototype UX reviewed; engineering scoping meeting scheduled 2026-07-01.

Operational notes / quick wins
- When running customer burst tests, prefer real traces over synthetic for cache behavior (notes from Liam). Add a small doc with steps to scrub traces before ingestion into staging (Omar to author).
- Add a 'schema compatibility' checklist item to the onboarding playbook — reduces repeat of Aurelia-style surprises (Priya to update playbook).

Action tracker (condensed)
- Priya: deliver preprocessor draft and test (Aurelia) — 2026-06-30
- Omar: dead-letter pipeline rule + scrubbed-trace doc — 2026-07-01
- Jason (SRE): instrument cache metrics by session id — 2026-07-01
- Liam: rollback per-session cache on canary + tradeoff doc PR#2876 — 2026-07-02
- Anita: confirm truncation allowance + produce HSM attestation (North Ridge) — 2026-07-02
- Marissa: schedule Aurelia schema sync + draft canary fallback runbook — 2026-06-30 / 2026-07-03
- Packaging (Vikram): minimal on-prem installer build — 2026-07-05
- Jason: CI deploy check for metadata hash divergence — 2026-07-06

Parking lot / longer-term
- Explore model-specific caching strategies (token vs prefix) with research team (longer-term).
- Consider a validation-as-a-service micro-tool to run customer schema checks before onboarding (product idea).

Meeting close / next sync
- Next weekly clearinghouse standup: 2026-07-06 10:00 PT (keep short; escalate if any High risks remain).
- Please update this doc inline if you make progress on your action items so we avoid duplicate work.

Raw notes / fragments captured during call:
- "If Aurelia won't change payload, we can do a short-living transform layer — but need an audit trail."
- "Crux trace will help — their chat session affinity is weird; maybe session ids rotate per request."
- "Packaging needs a whiteboard session ASAP to map binary dependencies to license risk."

End of notes.

-- Marissa
